interest: This file offers valuable insight into the global scope and commercial distribution networks of Japanese state and quasi-state propaganda at the onset of the Second Sino-Japanese War. It illustrates how business organizations like the Foreign Trade Association of Yokohama were leveraged to circulate Spanish-language justifications for military action to international trading bodies, reaching even the American Chamber of Commerce in Port-au-Prince, Haiti. The enclosed pamphlet is particularly useful for analyzing how Japan pitched its expansionist agenda to foreign commercial interests, framing military intervention as a reluctant defense of trade, law, and modernization against Chinese boycotts, violence, and the spread of Soviet communism, while specifically justifying aerial bombardments under the 1922 Hague air warfare rules.
overview: State Department decimal file 894.20238/1 consists of a January 4, 1938 diplomatic despatch from Ferdinand L. Mayer, the United States Minister in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, forwarding to the Secretary of State a Spanish-language propaganda pamphlet entitled '¿Por qué sucedió el actual incidente con la China?' ('Why Did the Present Incident with China Happen?'). The leaflet, addressed to the American Chamber of Commerce in Haiti and published by the Foreign Trade Association of Yokohama, Japan, sets forth the Japanese perspective on the outbreak of the Second Sino-Japanese War in 1937. It portrays Japanese military operations in North and Central China as justifiable acts of self-defense provoked by Chinese anti-Japanese policies, broken agreements, attacks on Japanese personnel, and Chiang Kai-shek's collaboration with communism, while appealing to foreign commercial communities to maintain harmonious trade relations with Japan.

subfiles.about: U.S. diplomatic despatch transmitting a Japanese propaganda leaflet received in Haiti.
subfiles.summary: Ferdinand L. Mayer, American Minister to Haiti, transmits to the Secretary of State in Washington a propaganda pamphlet received at the Legation in Port-au-Prince. The pamphlet was addressed to the American Chamber of Commerce in Haiti and sent ostensibly by the Foreign Trade Association of Yokohama, Japan. Mayer notes that the enclosed leaflet, entitled 'What Brought About the Actual Incident with China?', is forwarded as being of possible interest to the Department.

subfiles.about: Spanish-language propaganda leaflet presenting Japan's official justification for military operations in China during the Sino-Japanese conflict.
subfiles.from: Foreign Trade Association of Yokohama (La Asociación del Comercio Exterior de Yokohama)
subfiles.summary: This printed Spanish-language pamphlet, published by the Foreign Trade Association of Yokohama, justifies Japanese military actions in China following the outbreak of hostilities in 1937. It accuses the Chinese Nationalist government under Chiang Kai-shek of fostering anti-Japanese sentiment, violating treaties, boycotting Japanese goods, and allying with Soviet communism. Contrasting alleged chaos in China with order and prosperity in Manchukuo, the pamphlet blames Chinese forces for instigating clashes at the Marco Polo Bridge and Shanghai, denies reports of Japanese atrocities while defending air operations under the 1922 Hague rules, and appeals to foreign businessmen to maintain commercial ties with Japan.
subfiles.title: Pamphlet: '¿Porque sucedio el actual incidente con la China?' by the Foreign Trade Association of Yokohama
